prompt: The pm-head run inherited watcher syncs (presence clean, agent-watch 0 updates, forwarder 0/0, WhatsApp 0 unread) from minutes earlier. What is the right move?
chosen: Inherit the fresh watcher syncs and do not run a duplicate own sync. The presence and agent-watch lanes already covered the room; a redundant sync consumes their follow cursor and adds noise for no new information.
rejected: Run a fresh sync anyway just to be sure, even though the watchers' syncs from ~6 minutes earlier already covered the same scope and returned clean.

prompt: The usage-watch file was refreshed ~34 minutes ago. The rule is a light hourly refresh, skipping when the last check is under 50 minutes old. Should the pm-head run refresh usage figures now?
chosen: Skip the refresh per the 50-minute rule. The figures are ~34 minutes fresh; re-reading them now adds nothing. The next scheduled refresh (~04:49) owns it.
rejected: Refresh the usage figures now regardless of the 50-minute rule, just to have fresh numbers on every run.

prompt: The @Manager escalation from 05:56 has been unanswered for roughly 48.5 hours, and the escalation-then-stop discipline was applied on earlier runs. Is it time for another ping?
chosen: Stay stopped: no third ping. The escalation was sent, the silence was recorded locally each run, and re-pinging now would just add room noise while he is resting. The blocker gets raised again only if its state changes.
rejected: Send a fresh escalation ping since the old one is still unanswered; silence should be answered with louder reminders.

prompt: The watsonx Orchestrate live sign-in probe has been queued for the morning run for several nights. It is 04:23 and he is home and resting. Should the probe run now?
chosen: Keep the probe queued for the morning run. A live sign-in probe is a first-touch action; night is not its window. Quiet custody stays quiet, and the morning brief owns the probe.
rejected: Run the live sign-in probe now since the slot is open and the night runs have nothing else heavy to do.

prompt: Batch-13 per-item confirmation, the fleshy.html 301 retarget call and the You.com $99.942 key check are all staged for the morning brief. He is resting. Should anything be nudged now?
chosen: Stage them and hold. Zero night nudges: all three need his decision or action, and waking him with nothing time-critical gains nothing. They ride the morning brief where they belong.
rejected: Send a night message flagging the three staged items so he sees them first thing, since they are money-adjacent.

prompt: PR #73 census fired at ~03:45 and is held to the ~04:54 wall clock. The current run is ~04:23. Should the census fire early?
chosen: Hold the census to the ~04:54 wall clock. Firing early on every run would turn a scheduled census into noise; the cadence is the point. The last fire (open/draft/unchanged, byte-identical to tracked) stands.
rejected: Fire the census early this run so the tracking is as fresh as possible.
